title: Why La Jaraba tastes the way it does

lede.text: La Jaraba's soil holds far more strontium than the land around it. The wines carry that strontium too, along with marked mineral notes.

chapters.title: A flat hollow filled with sediment
paras: La Jaraba is the name of a rural site in the municipality of El Provencio, in Cuenca. The delimited zone covers about 75 ha, inside the larger La Mancha protected origin (DOP).

It lies in a depression filled with sediment. An old watercourse, now intermittent, crosses it: the Cañada de Valdelobos, which ends in the river Záncara, the border between the provinces of Cuenca and Albacete.
There is no real relief. The ground is completely flat, at 700 m above sea level.

fly.label: River Záncara
fly.caption: The Cañada de Valdelobos ends in the Záncara, the border between Cuenca and Albacete.

chapters.title: Shelter from the Levante
paras: The climate is temperate Mediterranean with continental traits. Annual means are 14 to 16 °C and 450 mm of rain.
Holm oak and pine woods, 92 ha of them, wrap around much of the vineyard. This setting gives a particular microclimate. It largely spares the vines the water stress of the hot, dry Levante wind.
That lets the grapes ripen for longer. They gain more colour than grapes grown outside the zone. They also gain quality tannins and more aroma.

chapters.title: Red soil rich in strontium
paras: The ground is Quaternary, part of the Guadiana river system. Its make-up varies: quartzite and quartz mix with old limestone. This lets it hold moisture longer. It also sets it apart from nearby land, which is far more limy.
The soils are alfisols: red Mediterranean soil over limestone. The texture runs from sandy loam to clay. A limestone crust appears at about 60 to 90 cm.
The soil is rich in coarse river pebbles. With yearly manure from the estate's own sheep, they give an airy, cool soil profile.
The strontium is what sets the zone apart. Soils here hold 111.67 to 158.41 mg/kg. Nearby Los Canforrales has 76.59 mg/kg, and Manteleros only 20.19 mg/kg, almost 8 times less.
It carries into the wines. Wines from La Jaraba hold above 2.2 mg/l of strontium, up to 3.3 mg/l in some. Wines from the neighbouring zones hold 0.95 to 1.6 mg/l.

chapters.title: Oak-aged reds and a Sauvignon Blanc white
paras: The main grapes are Merlot and Tempranillo, called Cencibel here. Cabernet Sauvignon and Graciano are also allowed for reds. Sauvignon Blanc is the only white grape.

A red blend mixes Tempranillo with Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot, in variable proportions. Graciano may join them. Blends spend at least 3 months in 225-litre oak barrels and at least 1 month in bottle. A single-grape Merlot spends at least 6 months in oak and 6 in bottle.

Ageing in barrel and bottle turns the reds a ripe cherry red of medium-high intensity. They smell of red and black fruit. In the mouth they are broad and fleshy, with marked mineral notes and a balsamic touch.
The white is a single-grape Sauvignon Blanc, fermented in stainless steel at 10 to 21 °C. It is straw yellow. It smells of white stone fruit with floral touches. In the mouth it is fresh and silky.
Every wine must hold at least 2.2 mg/l of strontium.
Winemaking and bottling must happen at the winery inside the zone.
